clue.text: Steal fitting placed on the M1 (South)

parts.note: the M1, Britain's first motorway, is written here with the figure one standing for the letter I
fitting means suitable, appropriate

explanation.surface: Someone describes a theft of fittings dumped on the southbound M1 motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main motorway north from London; its figure 1 doubles as the letter I. The brackets round South are only surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: To misappropriate is to take dishonestly for one's own use, a formal synonym for stealing.

clue.text: A reminder men hold me to

indicators.note: hold signals one group of letters gripping another, here the short words around the plural noun

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A keepsake that men clutch close to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The word order suggests the men do the holding, but 'hold' works the other way round: the two short words close around the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a souvenir kept as a reminder of a person or event.

clue.text: One helping to remove litter from the field

definitions.text: One helping to remove litter from the field

parts.words: One helping to remove litter from the field
parts.note: reads like a volunteer picking up rubbish after a match, but litter is an old word for a stretcher and the field is a battlefield or sports pitch

explanation.walkthrough: Litter here is a frame for carrying the injured, not rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretcher-bearers carry the wounded or injured off a battlefield or pitch on a litter.

clue.text: Soft butter bough: for baby

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
a butter is something that butts, such as a ram

explanation.surface: Gentle butter on a bough, laid out for a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but something that butts: a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: A pram is a baby carriage, so the phrase 'for baby' describes what it is used for.

clue.text: The rod becomes very heated

indicators.note: becomes signals that the letters of the two words turn into something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: A metal rod grows extremely hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-hot describes metal heated until it glows, so very heated.

clue.text: The place for a job

definitions.meaning: a place or location where something stands
a post or situation of employment

explanation.walkthrough: The scan's 'jcb' is a misread of 'job'.
explanation.definitionFit: Position means both the spot where something is and a post in employment.

clue.text: A rendition becoming excessive

indicators.note: becoming signals the letters of the phrase turning into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A performance of a song turns into something over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Inordinate means beyond reasonable limits, a synonym for excessive.

clue.text: How a hospital patient might have to accept

definitions.text: How a hospital patient might have to accept

parts.words: How a hospital patient might have to accept
parts.note: a bedridden patient literally receives things while flat in bed, and the idiom means to accept something without protest

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to submit to an insult or setback meekly, while a patient may literally be lying down.

clue.text: Fast river trapped journalist

indicators.note: trapped signals one piece being caught inside another

parts.note: the Spey is a Scottish river
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A rapid river caught a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spey is a salmon river in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedy is a plain synonym of fast, both meaning quick.

clue.text: She hasn't a leg to stand on

definitions.text: She hasn't a leg to stand on

parts.words: She hasn't a leg to stand on
parts.note: the idiom means someone has no valid argument, but taken literally it describes a sea creature with a fish's tail

explanation.definitionFit: A mermaid has a tail instead of legs, so literally has no leg to stand on.

clue.text: Accumulate shares that have increased in value?

definitions.meaning: to lay in supplies or build up a store

definitions.text: shares that have increased in value?
definitions.meaning: stock that has gone up in price

explanation.definitionFit: To stock up is to gather a store of supplies; read literally it is stock that has risen.

clue.text: Crackers-or what they're required for?

definitions.meaning: the things nutcrackers are needed to open

explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is slang for crazy, and nuts are what nutcrackers exist to crack.

clue.text: Signing-on points

parts.note: suggests places where one registers, but means the row of dots on a form where a signature goes

explanation.definitionFit: A dotted line is the series of dots on a document where you sign your name.

clue.text: NCO0 stripes for police officers

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'NCO0 stripes for police officers': NCO STRIPES is an anagram of the answer, but 'NCO0' is garbled and no anagram indicator survives; the clue as printed could not be found.

clue.text: Present for next-door

definitions.meaning: present in the sense of available or nearby
close at hand, in the immediate vicinity

explanation.definitionFit: On hand means available or present, and also close by, like something next door.

clue.text: Belittle blue entertainment

parts.note: blue means sad or depressed, down
a play is a theatrical entertainment

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a risque show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like smutty, describing the entertainment, but it means low in spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To downplay something is to make it seem less important, to belittle it.

clue.text: Can't have venison without a flask of wine

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: venison is the meat of deer
the apostrophe is dropped, leaving the letters of the word

explanation.surface: A diner refuses venison unless a flask of wine comes with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; the surface pretends someone refuses venison.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass vessel into which wine is poured for serving.

clue.text: Fought against being declared redundant

definitions.meaning: ... as in had a scrap, a fight
discarded or abandoned as no longer needed

explanation.definitionFit: Scrapped means both fought (had a scrap) and thrown out as useless.

clue.text: Hit on an advertising catch-phrase

indicators.note: on in a down clue places one piece on top of the next

parts.note: to slog is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A punchy line found for an ad campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' means placed above; the surface hit is a punch, not a success.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a memorable phrase used in advertising.

clue.text: Peels off in layers

definitions.meaning: long narrow bands or pieces of material

explanation.definitionFit: Strips means takes off as a verb, and as a noun long thin pieces or layers.

clue.text: Yet its operations don't take place here

definitions.text: Yet its operations don't take place here

parts.words: Yet its operations don't take place here
parts.note: a doctor's consulting room is named for operating, yet in Britain no operations are done there

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a GP's surgery is a local doctor's office where patients are seen, not operated on.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgery in British usage is a family doctor's consulting room, despite the name.

clue.text: In Latin 'I' is used by many showing vanity

parts.note: ego is the Latin word for I
taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: Constant use of the first person, even in Latin, reveals a conceited speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoism is self-centredness, close in sense to vanity.

clue.text: Make too many accusations of commercial malpractice

definitions.meaning: to lay too many charges against someone
asking a customer for more than a fair price

explanation.definitionFit: To overcharge is to bill too much, and could also mean to bring an excess of charges.

clue.text: I depart right after the operatic prince

indicators.note: after places the letter for right behind the other pieces

parts.note: to depart is to go

explanation.surface: A singer leaves once the opera's royal has finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Igor is the title role of Borodin's opera.

clue.text: An old-fashioned do

parts.note: suggests a quaint party, but means an archaic form of the verb to do

explanation.definitionFit: Doth is the archaic third-person singular of the verb do.

clue.text: Dry wine for those taking flight

parts.note: to air laundry is to dry it
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Dry wine served to travellers on a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' looks like an adjective describing the wine, but it is the verb air.
explanation.definitionFit: An airport is the place for people boarding flights.

clue.text: Raw material used in pig production

definitions.text: Raw material used in pig production

parts.words: Raw material used in pig production
parts.note: suggests farm animal feed, but pig is crude cast iron from a blast furnace

explanation.definitionFit: Pig iron is smelted from mined iron-bearing rock, its raw material.

clue.text: Round Tabler taking drink is booked

parts.note: Tristram is a knight of King Arthur's Round Table
shandy is beer mixed with lemonade

explanation.surface: A knight of the Round Table takes a drink and is reserved a table.
explanation.walkthrough: Shandy is a British pub drink of beer and lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristram Shandy is Laurence Sterne's novel, so it is a book.
